q2OtherPossibilities.text: I want to hear about some other possibilities.

q1.text: Before we begin, tell me what you'd like to learn. Not what you believe you're supposed to be good at, but what you genuinely wish to understand.
q1.speaker: mentor

q2.text: Now, answer honestly. I'm not looking for the answer you think I want to hear. What sort of life would you choose for yourself?
q2.speaker: mentor

q3.text: Let us imagine you've begun following that path. Something happens that requires a decision, and the choice is yours to make. How would you respond?
q3.speaker: mentor

q4.text: Very well. Now consider something different. What served you before may not serve you here, so tell me what you would do.
q4.speaker: mentor

q5.text: You needn't know every step of your journey today. Even the most certain among us can find ourselves somewhere unexpected. But tell me, who do you hope to become?
q5.speaker: mentor

q1.text: Inquiry: Master, which of your abilities would you most like to cultivate? I can assess your aptitudes with considerable accuracy. Your personal interests, however, require your input.
q1.speaker: mentor

q2.text: Observation: The most efficient career is not necessarily the most fulfilling one, Master. I would be interested to know which profession you would choose for yourself.
q2.speaker: mentor

q3.text: Hypothetical Scenario: Let us assume you have successfully entered your chosen profession, Master. An unexpected complication has arisen. How would you prefer to resolve it?
q3.speaker: mentor

q4.text: Cautionary Observation: A different set of circumstances now requires your attention, Master. I advise against assuming that a familiar approach is always the correct one. How would you proceed?
q4.speaker: mentor

q5.text: Personal Admission: I can calculate the probability of your success, Master. I find myself rather more concerned with whether that success would make you happy. Who do you hope to become?
q5.speaker: mentor

q1.text: Arr! Pick yer path wisely, matey! The right tricks make the difference between a chest o' credits and a long walk out a short airlock.
q1.speaker: mentor

q2.text: Every spacer's chasin' somethin', matey. Credits, glory, freedom, maybe a ship worth callin' yer own. So tell ol' Salty, what sort o' life are ye chartin' a course for?
q2.speaker: mentor

q3.text: A fancy ship won't save ye if ye can't lie, sneak, or think fast! Now, every good job's got a way o' turnin' sour. Let's see how ye'd handle a little trouble.
q3.speaker: mentor

q4.text: Yar! But there ain't just one kind o' trouble in this galaxy, matey. Let's throw another scrape yer way and see if ye've got the wits to sail through it!
q4.speaker: mentor

q5.text: Credits come and go, but reputation sticks, matey. One day they'll be tellin' stories about ye in cantinas from here to the Outer Rim. What d'ye want those stories to say?
q5.speaker: mentor

q1.text: You can't be good at everything. Anyone who tells you otherwise is either lying or about to become a casualty. So, where do you want to put your effort?
q1.speaker: mentor

q2.text: Training gives you options. It doesn't give you a reason to use them. What sort of work are you actually interested in?
q2.speaker: mentor

q3.text: All right. Let's put you in that line of work for a moment. Tell me what you'd actually do in this situation, not what you think I want to hear.
q3.speaker: mentor

q4.text: Different terrain. Different problem. What changes in your approach?
q4.speaker: mentor

q5.text: People can spend years getting very good at a job they never intended to do. It happens. Where do you actually want to end up?
q5.speaker: mentor

q1.text: Pick what feels right in your hands. Doesn't have to be a cannon, though I recommend one! So, what do you want to get good at?
q1.speaker: mentor

q2.text: Everybody's got their work. What do you want yours to be?
q2.speaker: mentor

q3.text: All right, say you've got that job, and already something's gone wrong. What do you do?
q3.speaker: mentor

q4.text: Now here's a different mess. Bigger guns won't fix every problem, much to my disappointment. What would you try?
q4.speaker: mentor

q5.text: I know what I want. Keep my people safe, make sure they've got something worth living for. What about you? What do you want to make of yourself?
q5.speaker: mentor

prompt.text: What kind of Jedi would you most like to develop into?
prompt.speaker: mentor

options.text: I want to become a Jedi Guardian, developing the strength and courage to face danger and protect others.

I'm not sure yet. I would like to explore what the Force and my training have to offer before choosing a path.

jedi.text: I want to help found a settlement where people can live safely, using patience and cooperation to turn unfamiliar ground into a home.

noble.text: I want to establish a new colony, organizing settlers, supplies, and institutions so the community can endure.

scoundrel.text: I want to help build a colony from spare parts and stubbornness, making a fresh start where nobody tells us how to live.

scout.text: I want to scout a place for a new settlement, learn its hazards, and help its first inhabitants survive the frontier.

soldier.text: I want to help establish a colony, securing its perimeter and teaching settlers how to protect the home we build together.

universalReference.text: I want to track dangerous creatures into their own territory and learn how to survive the hunt.

jedi.text: I want to learn the ways of dangerous beasts, tracking them with care and confronting them only when the hunt demands it.

noble.text: I want to organize expeditions to hunt formidable creatures, studying their habits before anyone risks entering their territory.

scoundrel.text: I want to make a name hunting beasts that scare other people away, finding the trail and getting out with my prize.

scout.text: I want to track dangerous creatures through their own territory, learning their habits well enough to survive every encounter.

soldier.text: I want to hunt powerful beasts, preparing for their strength and meeting them with discipline instead of panic.

universalReference.text: I want to understand and care for creatures others fear, earning their trust and learning to work alongside them.

jedi.text: I want to understand creatures that others fear, earning their trust through patience rather than forcing them to obey.

noble.text: I want to care for and train animals, learning how to manage their needs and work with them responsibly.

scoundrel.text: I want to get along with creatures that would bite anyone else, learning what makes them tick and how to earn their cooperation.

scout.text: I want to read an animal's behavior and care for it in the field, building trust even far from familiar surroundings.

soldier.text: I want to learn to handle and care for working beasts, keeping them calm and reliable when the situation turns dangerous.

universalReference.text: I want to form a bond with a mount and learn to travel and fight as though we were one.

jedi.text: I want to train alongside a mount until we trust one another completely, learning to move through danger as partners.

noble.text: I want to master riding and care for a mount, learning the confidence and control needed to travel with it anywhere.

scoundrel.text: I want to ride a beast that can take me where engines cannot, building enough trust that we can get out of trouble together.

scout.text: I want to bond with a riding beast and cross difficult country together, learning its pace, instincts, and limits.

soldier.text: I want to train with a war mount, learning to maneuver and fight as a team without putting the animal at needless risk.

universalReference.text: I want to shape the stories people believe, using words and images to rally support for the causes I serve.

jedi.text: I want to shape public understanding through speeches and stories, persuading people to support a cause I believe in.

noble.text: I want to direct campaigns of public messaging, choosing the words and images that can move opinion toward my cause.

scoundrel.text: I want to know how to sell a story to a crowd, turning a clever message into the support my cause needs.

scout.text: I want to bring firsthand accounts from distant places to the wider galaxy, using them to rally people behind a cause.

soldier.text: I want to craft messages that keep people committed to a cause, making sure the public understands why the struggle matters.

universalReference.text: I want to help overthrow an unjust order, then build a government that won't repeat its mistakes.

jedi.text: I want to help replace an oppressive government, then work with others to build a fairer order that lasts beyond the rebellion.

noble.text: I want to lead political change, bringing down unjust institutions and helping write the laws that replace them.

scoundrel.text: I want to outmaneuver a corrupt regime and help build a new government that cannot be bought as easily as the old one.

scout.text: I want to carry a revolution beyond the capital, listening to distant communities and giving them a voice in what comes next.

soldier.text: I want to fight to end an unjust regime, then help create a government worthy of the sacrifices people made.

universalReference.text: I want to unite my beliefs with martial discipline, defending what I hold sacred through counsel or force when needed.

jedi.text: I want to join a sacred martial tradition, deepening my beliefs while learning when to offer counsel and when to defend them.

noble.text: I want to serve as a warrior-priest, guiding a community through faith and standing beside it when violence threatens.

scoundrel.text: I want to find a cause sacred enough to live by and learn the fighting skills to defend it when words fail.

scout.text: I want to follow a spiritual warrior tradition, carrying its teachings across distant places and protecting those who share them.

soldier.text: I want to bind my combat training to a sacred duty, serving as both a defender and a spiritual guide.

universalReference.text: I want to wield the dark side from the shadows, slipping past defenses and striking before an enemy knows I'm there.

jedi.text: I want to follow the path of a Sith Assassin, learning to hide my approach and draw upon the dark side to defeat a target unseen.

noble.text: I want to pursue Sith Assassin training, using secrecy and the dark side to remove obstacles without announcing my intentions.

scoundrel.text: I want to become a Sith Assassin, combining a silent approach with forbidden Force training to strike before anyone is ready.

scout.text: I want to learn the Sith Assassin's methods, tracking a target through shadows and seeking the dark-side skills to close in unseen.

soldier.text: I want to train as a Sith Assassin, adding infiltration and dark-side techniques to the discipline of a precise strike.

universalReference.text: I want to delve into forbidden Force lore and alchemy, mastering powers that others are too fearful to study.

jedi.text: I want to become a Sith Sorcerer, studying dark-side lore and alchemy until I can wield powers few dare to seek.

noble.text: I want to gather forbidden knowledge and pursue Sith sorcery, learning how its rituals and alchemy are practiced.

scoundrel.text: I want to seek out the secrets of Sith sorcery, following dangerous leads until I learn the dark arts others avoid.

scout.text: I want to travel to forgotten sites to study Sith sorcery, uncovering the lore and rituals hidden beyond known space.

soldier.text: I want to study Sith sorcery and alchemy, pursuing a kind of power that battlefield training alone cannot provide.

universalReference.text: I want to use the dark side to bend hearts and decisions, gaining influence without needing to draw a blade.

jedi.text: I want to master Sith manipulation, studying how the dark side can influence minds and turn decisions in my favor.

noble.text: I want to become a Sith Manipulator, using influence and dark-side study to control decisions from behind the scenes.

scoundrel.text: I want to learn the Sith Manipulator's arts, mixing deceit with dark-side power until people choose what I want them to choose.

scout.text: I want to follow the hidden workings of Sith influence, learning how to manipulate rivals without openly confronting them.

soldier.text: I want to pursue Sith manipulation, gaining the influence to turn adversaries against one another before a battle begins.

universalReference.text: I want to devote myself to a secret dark-side tradition, learning its rituals and preserving the power it promises.

jedi.text: I want to join a dark-side tradition outside the familiar orders, learning its rites and understanding the power its members seek.

noble.text: I want to belong to a secret dark-side cult, studying its teachings and helping preserve its rituals across generations.

scoundrel.text: I want to find a hidden dark-side order and learn the rituals its members keep from the rest of the galaxy.

scout.text: I want to seek out an isolated dark-side tradition, traveling to its hidden sanctuaries to learn its practices.

soldier.text: I want to enter a dark-side cult and train within its rites, learning what its teachings demand of those who follow them.

universalReference.text: I want to live beyond the reach of the Jedi and Sith, discovering what the Force means to me on my own terms.

jedi.text: I want to leave the Jedi and Sith behind, seeking a life where I can understand the Force without obeying either order.

noble.text: I want to live beyond the influence of Jedi and Sith institutions, seeking my own understanding of the Force and my place in the galaxy.

scoundrel.text: I want to stay clear of Jedi and Sith alike, chasing my own answers about the Force without letting either side claim me.

scout.text: I want to travel far from the great Force orders, exploring unfamiliar traditions and deciding for myself what the Force means.

soldier.text: I want to find an independent path with the Force, keeping my freedom instead of taking orders from Jedi or Sith.

universalReference.text: I want to seek a deeper connection with the Force through meditation, tradition, and experiences beyond ordinary understanding.

jedi.text: I want to explore the Force through meditation and reflection, learning what quieter experiences can reveal beyond combat training.

noble.text: I want to seek instruction in the Force's mysteries, studying traditions that value contemplation and inner understanding.

scoundrel.text: I want to discover what the Force really means, following strange traditions and learning to be still long enough to listen.

scout.text: I want to explore remote traditions of the Force, finding places and teachers that deepen my understanding of its mysteries.

soldier.text: I want to pursue the Force through study and meditation, learning a discipline that goes beyond the drills I already know.

universalReference.text: I want to learn to read visions and warnings in the Force, guiding my choices by what I sense may come.

jedi.text: I want to study visions of the Force, learning to recognize warnings without letting fear of the future decide everything.

noble.text: I want to seek the gift of foresight through the Force, learning to interpret signs that might help me guide others.

scoundrel.text: I want to learn how to read glimpses of the future through the Force, knowing when to trust a warning and when to question it.

scout.text: I want to follow signs and visions in the Force, learning to recognize dangers before anyone else can see them.

soldier.text: I want to study Force visions and foresight, learning how an early warning might keep people alive when plans fail.

universalReference.text: I want to bring the Force into battle, sharpening my instincts and strength until my fighting becomes an extension of it.

jedi.text: I want to train as a Force Warrior, joining disciplined combat with the Force until each strengthens the other.

noble.text: I want to seek Force Warrior training, learning to combine martial skill with Force techniques rather than relying on status alone.

scoundrel.text: I want to become a Force Warrior, adding hard-earned Force training to the fighting instincts that keep me moving.

scout.text: I want to pursue the Force Warrior's path, blending field instincts and mobility with the Force in a fight.

soldier.text: I want to develop as a Force Warrior, bringing the Force into combat without forgetting discipline and teamwork.

universalReference.text: I want to practice the Force through ancient rites and the natural world, learning the mysteries preserved by those who came before me.

jedi.text: I want to learn the ways of a Force Witch, studying ancient rites and the bond between the Force and the living world.

noble.text: I want to seek a Force Witch tradition, learning its rituals and helping preserve the knowledge passed through its practitioners.

scoundrel.text: I want to follow the Force Witch's old practices, finding the teachers and secrets others dismiss as superstition.

scout.text: I want to study Force Witch traditions among wild places and distant peoples, learning how they work with the living world.

soldier.text: I want to pursue Force Witch training, learning the rites and field wisdom of a tradition far from ordinary military life.

situation.text: An evacuation is underway when hostile raiders break through a station's security doors. Several civilians are trapped in an exposed corridor, and the people covering their escape are beginning to fall back. You are close enough to intervene, but you cannot be everywhere at once.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would hold the corridor and give the civilians time to escape.
I would draw the raiders away from the trapped people and keep them focused on me.
I would try to convince the raiders to stop, even if it only buys us a moment.
I would look for another route and help the civilians through it before confronting anyone.
I would organize the retreat so the defenders and civilians can move together.

situation.text: A remote outpost's emergency beacon has stopped broadcasting just as its security systems begin behaving unpredictably. The technicians suspect sabotage, while the frightened residents insist something stranger is happening. You have limited time before the next transport arrives.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would examine the security controls and trace where the failures began.
I would question the technicians and residents separately to find what their stories have in common.
I would secure the most dangerous systems first so no one gets hurt while we investigate.
I would quietly search for signs that someone deliberately interfered with the outpost.
I would bring the frightened residents together and help them organize a response.

situation.text: Two groups sheltering in a storm-damaged enclave both claim the only functioning medical station. Their representatives are arguing, injured people are waiting, and no one trusts the other side to distribute care fairly.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would bring the two groups together and work toward a fair arrangement for treating the injured.
I would help the most critically injured people first and let the argument wait.
I would ask what each group fears losing, then look for a compromise they can trust.
I would organize a clear treatment schedule and ask both groups to help enforce it.
I would investigate whether another space or set of supplies could serve as a second care station.

situation.text: Small objects have vanished from a frontier settlement, and a young resident has now gone missing. The local authorities blame an outsider, but the few witnesses contradict one another and someone has tampered with the security logs.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would retrace the missing resident’s last movements and examine the places they visited.
I would question the witnesses calmly and compare the details they remember.
I would study the altered security logs and look for whoever had access to them.
I would keep watch near the likely next target and wait to see who appears.
I would protect the accused outsider while gathering enough evidence to challenge the accusation.

situation.text: During a confrontation in a crowded hangar, an armed opponent challenges you at close range. Cargo, machinery, and fleeing workers limit your movement, and a reckless attack could put others in danger.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would keep my movements controlled and use the space around us to defend against each strike.
I would maneuver the opponent away from the workers before committing to the fight.
I would try to end the confrontation through words before either of us swings.
I would look for a chance to disarm the opponent rather than injure them.
I would guide the workers toward safety and let my allies create room for us to act.

situation.text: During your first assignment away from familiar surroundings, a settlement reports a disturbance near its power station. The equipment is malfunctioning, residents are frightened, and a security patrol is demanding immediate action. No one agrees on what caused the problem.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would inspect the failing equipment and work out what is actually wrong.
I would speak with the residents and compare what each person saw.
I would keep people clear of the power station until we know whether it is safe.
I would ask the security patrol to coordinate with the technicians instead of acting blindly.
I would quietly observe the area for anything that does not belong there.

situation.text: You are asked to organize a small group evacuating a damaged transit hub. Two volunteers disagree over who should lead, one exit is blocked, and frightened passengers are beginning to scatter.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would assign people clear tasks and get the evacuation moving before the disagreement spreads.
I would hear both volunteers out and win their cooperation before choosing a plan.
I would check the blocked exit and identify the safest available route.
I would work with the frightened passengers directly and keep them moving in small groups.
I would ask the volunteers to lead separate jobs so both can contribute without fighting for control.

situation.text: A patrol has halted your group's passage through a checkpoint after a misunderstanding over travel authorization. The officer is suspicious, one companion is growing angry, and a crowd is forming behind you.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would calmly explain the misunderstanding and ask what proof would satisfy the officer.
I would stop my companion from escalating matters and make sure we present one clear account.
I would review our documents and look for a legitimate authorization the officer overlooked.
I would find out what the officer is concerned about and offer a practical way to address it.
I would ask for a supervisor or neutral official before the crowd makes the situation worse.

situation.text: A supply convoy has two possible routes to a cut-off community. The faster route is exposed to raiders; the safer road may be blocked by a recent landslide. You have incomplete maps and only enough fuel to commit to one route.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would compare the routes, estimate the risks, and choose the one most likely to get us through.
I would send a small reconnaissance team to confirm whether the supposedly safer road is open.
I would talk with local guides and drivers before trusting the incomplete maps.
I would organize the convoy to handle an ambush if we have to take the exposed route.
I would look for a way to reduce our load or conserve fuel so we have more than one option.

situation.text: Essential supplies keep disappearing from a relief depot, yet every inventory report claims the shipments are complete. The depot supervisor is unusually defensive, several workers know more than they admit, and openly accusing anyone could shut down cooperation.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would examine the shipment records and follow the inconsistencies until they point somewhere.
I would speak privately with the workers and earn enough trust to learn what they know.
I would put a new inventory process in place and see when the losses stop.
I would quietly observe the depot during deliveries to catch the theft as it happens.
I would bring in a trusted outside reviewer so no one can dismiss the findings as a personal accusation.

situation.text: A small community needs replacement parts for its failing water system. Several potential supporters are willing to help, but each wants a different public commitment in return, and residents disagree over whose offer to accept.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would negotiate support without promising the community something it cannot accept.
I would invite residents to decide which commitments they are willing to make.
I would approach more supporters so no one donor can dictate the terms.
I would examine the actual repair needs and ask for only the resources that matter most.
I would publicly explain every offer so the community can judge the tradeoffs.

situation.text: At a community meeting, residents demand help after a transport accident. Officials blame one another, the affected families want answers, and resources are limited. You are invited to help move the discussion forward.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would give the families a chance to speak and make sure their concerns shape the response.
I would identify the resources available and organize immediate help for those affected.
I would ask the officials to state what they know, what they do not, and who will investigate.
I would work out a short list of decisions the group can make right now.
I would speak privately with the people arguing and look for common ground.

situation.text: The freighter you're traveling on drops out of hyperspace farther from its destination than expected. A patrol vessel is approaching, the navigation readings are inconsistent, and the crew is arguing over whether to run, hide, or make contact.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would check the ship’s instruments and find out whether the navigation error is getting worse.
I would take the controls and look for a route that keeps us out of the patrol’s path.
I would contact the patrol and talk us through the encounter without revealing more than necessary.
I would have the crew prepare a convincing explanation while I work out what the patrol wants.
I would get everyone working together on our position, fuel, and escape options before making a move.

situation.text: A routine exchange at a crowded gaming hall suddenly turns against you when your contact changes the terms and quietly signals two associates to block the exits. You have seconds to decide whether the situation can be turned around or abandoned.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would keep talking, act confident, and see whether I can make the contact doubt their own advantage.
I would look for a distraction and slip toward an exit before the trap closes.
I would study the associates and work out which one is least committed to the plan.
I would turn the deal into a new bargain that gives the contact a reason to let me go.
I would signal my companions to cover the exits while I keep the contact occupied.

situation.text: Blaster fire erupts inside a busy maintenance bay. The attackers are using machinery for cover, a companion is pinned down, and workers are trying to escape across your line of sight.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would take careful shots at the attackers when the workers are clear of my line of fire.
I would move around the machinery and force the attackers to watch more than one angle.
I would lay down covering fire so my companion can get out of danger.
I would look for a way to shut down the machinery or lights and disrupt the attackers’ advantage.
I would call out a route for the workers and coordinate our escape instead of staying to trade shots.

situation.text: A suspicious docking official demands paperwork your group cannot immediately produce. A companion is about to offer an obviously contradictory explanation, and the official's hand is moving toward a security alarm.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would take over the conversation and give the official a story they can accept.
I would ask what authorization we need and try to negotiate a legitimate way through.
I would interrupt my companion before the contradictions give us away.
I would distract the official long enough for someone else to find the missing paperwork.
I would look for a reason to withdraw politely and return when we are better prepared.

situation.text: A warehouse security lockdown seals the door to your group's escape route. The control terminal still has power, but its access permissions have been changed; nearby machinery might provide another way through if you can work quickly.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would work through the terminal and try to restore the access permissions.
I would inspect the nearby machinery for a mechanical way around the locked door.
I would search for a maintenance route instead of fighting the security system.
I would find the sensor or alarm causing the lockdown and work out how to isolate it.
I would organize the group to keep watch and clear a path while I tackle the problem.

situation.text: A simple delivery job falls apart when the intended recipient vanishes, the promised payment is missing, and someone begins asking questions about your cargo. You have a few minutes to decide what to do next.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would find out who last saw the recipient and follow the trail before it goes cold.
I would keep the cargo out of sight until I know who is asking about it.
I would contact whoever hired me and negotiate a new arrangement before taking another risk.
I would check the cargo for anything that explains why everyone suddenly cares about it.
I would gather my companions, compare what we know, and decide whether to leave immediately.

situation.text: Your group is ambushed while crossing a narrow ravine. The attackers control the main trail, the nearest cover is scattered along the slope, and staying where you are leaves everyone exposed.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would move from cover to cover and find an angle the attackers have not secured.
I would study the ravine and identify a safe route for everyone to retreat.
I would use careful return fire to keep the attackers occupied while the group moves.
I would climb toward a better observation point and find out how many attackers there are.
I would coordinate a quick push to the nearest defensible position instead of scattering.

situation.text: A sudden storm destroys your group's navigation equipment in unfamiliar wilderness. Night is approaching, drinking water is running low, and the most obvious route back crosses unstable ground.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would find shelter and secure clean water before attempting a dangerous route in the dark.
I would study the terrain and weather for a safer path back.
I would inventory our gear and make the supplies last until conditions improve.
I would scout ahead for a landmark or a place to signal for help.
I would organize the group so no one becomes exhausted or separated while we move.

situation.text: From an observation point, you spot an enemy lookout signaling toward a nearby camp. Your position gives you a partial view, but distance, cover, and moving figures make an immediate shot uncertain.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would wait for a clear line of sight and take a shot only if I can identify the target.
I would keep observing to learn who the lookout is signaling and what the camp is preparing.
I would change position quietly to improve my view without exposing the group.
I would alert my companions and plan a coordinated response before anyone acts.
I would look for a way to bypass the lookout entirely and avoid starting a fight.

situation.text: A search party has failed to return from the foothills. You find two sets of tracks leading away from their last camp, but heavy rain is erasing the signs and one trail approaches dangerous cliffs.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would examine both trails for signs that show which searchers went where.
I would check the cliff route first from a safe vantage point in case someone is trapped there.
I would speak with anyone who saw the party leave and compare their account with the tracks.
I would divide the search into clear responsibilities so we can cover ground without losing anyone.
I would establish a safe route back before chasing either trail deeper into the hills.

situation.text: You are helping bring a shuttle down near a remote landing site when a dust storm reduces visibility. One approach is shorter but crosses rough terrain; the other is longer, and the ship's fuel reserve is shrinking.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would rely on the instruments and make the approach that gives us the most reliable readings.
I would circle to study the storm and find a safer opening before descending.
I would assess the shuttle’s fuel and decide how much time we can afford to spend searching.
I would ask the crew to help track terrain and hazards while I manage the approach.
I would look for another landing site rather than force the shuttle into a dangerous descent.

situation.text: Your group reaches an unmarked crossing and discovers the route ahead has been damaged by a flood. Supplies are limited, an unfamiliar signal is coming from beyond the crossing, and the group needs a way forward.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would inspect the damaged crossing and decide whether any part of it is still safe to use.
I would follow the unfamiliar signal far enough to learn whether it means help or danger.
I would scout along the floodplain for another place to cross.
I would organize a temporary camp and conserve supplies while we assess our options.
I would ask everyone what they have noticed before committing the group to a route.

situation.text: A hostile armored vehicle is covering an approach to an evacuation corridor. A mounted heavy weapon is available nearby, but its firing lane is narrow, ammunition is limited, and civilians are still moving through the area.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would use controlled bursts to force the vehicle back while the civilians clear the lane.
I would hold fire until I have a shot that does not put the evacuees at risk.
I would organize the evacuation so the civilians are out of the firing lane before we engage.
I would look for a weak point in the vehicle’s position instead of spending ammunition blindly.
I would work with the other defenders to distract the vehicle and move the civilians through another route.

situation.text: Your team is retreating through a damaged checkpoint when enemy fire cuts off the rear group. An injured teammate cannot move quickly, and the only solid cover is too far away to protect everyone at once.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would move to protect the injured teammate and buy them time to reach cover.
I would cover the rear group while the others organize a safer withdrawal.
I would identify the safest route and direct each teammate toward it in turn.
I would move around the attackers and draw their attention away from the wounded.
I would check what cover or equipment we can reposition to shield the retreat.

situation.text: Enemy fighters are firing from several windows overlooking a narrow street. Your squad must cross, but only brief glimpses reveal where the hostile fire is coming from, and ammunition is running low.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would watch the windows and wait for clear shots instead of wasting ammunition.
I would coordinate covering fire so the squad can cross in stages.
I would move to another angle and force the attackers to abandon their positions.
I would identify which window is controlling the street and concentrate our attention there.
I would look for a protected route around the street rather than fight on the enemy’s terms.

situation.text: A hostile boarder blocks the only accessible passage off a damaged ship compartment. The corridor is cramped, a ruptured fuel line makes stray blaster fire hazardous, and an ally needs you to clear a path.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would close the distance carefully and force the boarder away from the passage.
I would hold the boarder’s attention while my ally finds a way past.
I would use the cramped space to pin the opponent long enough to clear the corridor.
I would search for a hatch or maintenance route that lets us avoid the confrontation.
I would coordinate with my ally to create an opening instead of facing the boarder alone.

situation.text: Two members of your squad disagree about how to withdraw from a compromised position. Communications with command are down, the extraction window is closing, and the rest of the team is waiting for direction.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would make the call, give everyone a clear role, and start the withdrawal immediately.
I would hear both plans quickly and choose the one that protects the most teammates.
I would scout the escape route before risking the whole squad on it.
I would organize covering positions so everyone can move without being left behind.
I would focus first on anyone injured or cut off, then build the withdrawal around getting them out.

situation.text: A remote outpost has taken damage during a surprise attack. One person is wounded, a defense system has failed, and scouts report that the attackers may return soon. The available team can only address one immediate problem at a time.
situation.speaker: mentor

replies.text: I would get the wounded person to safety and arrange immediate care.
I would restore or defend the broken security system before another attack.
I would organize everyone into a clear plan with jobs they can carry out.
I would scout the surrounding area to learn how close the attackers really are.
I would reposition the defenders and prepare the outpost for another assault.

situation.text: A customs cruiser orders your freighter to dock just before a delivery deadline. Your cargo is valuable, your papers are incomplete, and your client insists the shipment must arrive today.
situation.speaker: mentor

children.text: I'd use speed, forged timing, and a carefully chosen route to slip the cargo past inspection.

methods.text: I'd create a believable explanation that gives us room to maneuver.
I'd reassess the route and handle the craft with precision.
I'd listen to the people involved and build useful relationships.
I'd consider the routes, vessels, and risks before making a move.
I'd ask careful questions and compare what different people know.

situation.text: A remote settlement offers you shelter if you can help reopen a dangerous route to its supply cache. Locals disagree about which paths are safe, and the weather is worsening.
situation.speaker: mentor

children.text: I'd look for an unconventional path through the frontier and rely on the people I meet along the way.

methods.text: I'd survey unfamiliar ground and learn what options are available.
I'd observe the details others might miss before making a move.
I'd secure food, shelter, and safety before taking unnecessary risks.
I'd use fieldcraft to keep everyone safe in the conditions.
I'd keep going through the hardship while others recover.

situation.text: Two ports offer lucrative markets for your shipment, but each demands a different concession and your crew cannot afford to visit both. Your investors want an immediate decision.
situation.speaker: mentor

children.text: I'd inspect the machinery, salvage what is useful, and negotiate a trade built around working parts.
I'd call on trusted port contacts and settle on terms that keep the trade fair for both sides.
I'd spot the overlooked value in a pile of scrap and turn it into a useful bargain.

methods.text: I'd research the underlying problem before trusting an easy answer.
I'd speak to the people involved and search for agreement.
I'd listen to the people involved and build useful relationships.
